text:
jen: Quick brainstorm for the micro-bbenchmark launch creative. Need: 1) a crisp 1-line social hook, 2) three visuals for hero + blog, 3) webinar outline, 4) demo/form routing + lead scoring. Short thoughts?

omar: Audience = engineers evaluating hosted vs dedicated, and platform teams sizing infra. Tone: numbers-first, no fluff.

rachel: Visuals idea: panel A = cost breakdown per 1M tokens with and without caching/batching; panel B = latency percentiles across 8 seq lengths (line stacks); panel C = "dollars per 1k requests" vs TPS scatter with clear callouts for two model families.

kai: Chart specs I can hand off:
```
1) stacked bars: y=$ / 1M tokens, series=[base, batching, cache, quantization]
2) percentile lines: x=seq_len, y=latency-ms, series=[p50,p95,p99]
3) scatter: x=reqs/s, y=$/1k-reqs, color=deployment-type, size=median-latency
```
Keep annotations: annotate the knee points where batching stops helping.

mara: Hero hook options:
- "Lower cost per inference. Same or better latency."
- "Planable unit cost. Measurable latency."
- "Make predictions cheaper, not slower."
I like the first but reworded: "Lower inference cost without slowing responses."

jen: Short social variant for hero: "Lower inference cost. Same speed. See how." Don't use words like "warmpath" or internal ops.

omar: Webinar: 35 minutes. 8m problem framing (why unit economics are the new SLA), 15m walkthrough of the three charts with live scenario (pre-filled QPS), 7m customer mini-case, 5m live Q&A. Outcome: CTA -> run an interactive estimator or schedule ops review.

rachel: For the interactive estimator: form fields: 1) avg seq length (dropdown), 2) projected peak reqs/s (buckets), 3) current model family (dropdown), 4) deployment preference (hosted/dedicated/private). Hidden fields: utm_campaign=microbench_q2_2026. Tag submissions with "bench_calc".

kai: Lead routing rules: if deployment=private OR peak_reqs_s > 1500 -> route to SDR queue labeled "bench-high-priority". Else -> growth funnel email + product nurture. Also add a low-friction "book ops review" checkbox that escalates.

mara: CTA shortlist: ["Run the estimator", "Estimate your costs", "Book an ops review"]. Primary: "Run the estimator". Secondary inline: "Book an ops review".

jen: Ads note (ads-bot, can you confirm): we should A/B creative: one variant emphasizes $/1k requests, the other emphasizes 99th latency. Targeting: devs, infra architects, ML platform.

ads-bot: Confirmed. Will spin up two creatives, track clicks->calc_submitted. Audience: lookalike from product-signups + job titles: "ML Engineer", "Platform Engineer".

omar: Copy for blog launch (short paragraph to lead into charts):
"Inference decisions are rarely binary. Teams balance latency, cost, and predictability. Our micro-benchmarks show how batching, caching, and model choices move the needle in real workloads — and where tradeoffs show up at tail percentiles. Below are three visual slices to help you map your numbers. Run the estimator to see a projection for your traffic."

rachel: Microcopy for social posts: 1) "How much could inference actually cost you? Run a quick estimate." 2) "See where latency shows up — and how to stop it from costing you." Keep <120 char.

kai: Operational checklist: export CSVs for each chart slice, upload PNGs to CDN, add alt text describing axis and key callouts, link estimator API endpoint with prefill params from form. Share CSVs with docs team for appendix.

mara: A/B test plan: hero CTA variant A = "Run the estimator" (primary), B = "Estimate your costs". Measure CTR -> calc_submitted conversion over 2 weeks. Use UTMs: utm_campaign=microbench_q2_2026, utm_content=heroA/heroB.

jen: Timeline: kai will deliver chart assets + CSV by EOD today, rachel will draft blog + captions by 6pm, omar to draft social ad copy by 3pm, ads-bot to queue ad tests, mara to update form and routing rules. We reconvene at 2026-03-25 09:30 PT for final signoff.

ads-bot: Meeting created: "Microbench launch sync" 2026-03-25 09:30 PT.

jen: Great work team. Reminder: public-facing material = numbers + tradeoffs, keep implementation details for the appendix/technical whitepaper. :rocket:
